ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two memory chips labeled “256 Bytes”, respectively Chip #1 and Chip #2. On the left side of each chip, A0-A7 address lines are connected, indicating that each chip internally uses 8 address lines to address 256 bytes. In the middle there are two chip-select decoding gates, whose inputs come from A8 and A9, and are respectively connected to the CS select terminals of the two chips. The bottom marks A10-A15 not used, indicating that these high-order address lines do not enter the chips' internal address inputs, and also do not directly participate in the decoding of the two chip-select gates in the figure. Reasoning: Because each chip only uses A0-A7, each selected chip corresponds to a 256-byte range. Decode A9 and A8 according to the chip-select logic in the figure: Chip #1 is selected when A9=1 and A8=1; Chip #2 is selected when A9=1 and A8=0. Therefore when A9=0, regardless of whether A8 is 0 or 1, and regardless of how A0-A7 vary, neither chip will be selected. In the high address block corresponding to the problem, A15..A10 are fixed as 111110, set A9=0, A8 may be 0 or 1, and A7..A0 vary from 00000000 to 11111111. The lowest-end bit pattern is 1111 1000 0000 0000, namely F800; the highest-end bit pattern is 1111 1001 1111 1111, namely F9FF. So the address range not represented by Chip #1 and Chip #2 is F800 to F9FF.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A0-A7 go into each 256-byte chip as internal address inputs, while A8 and A9 feed the chip-select decoding gates; A10-A15 are not part of the chip address inputs. Decode the CS logic as a truth table over A9 and A8. Chip #1 is selected when A9=1 and A8=1; chip #2 is selected when A9=1 and A8=0. Therefore any address with A9=0 selects neither chip, regardless of A8 and regardless of A0-A7. In the relevant high-address block, set A15..A10 to the fixed high bits and let A9=0, A8 vary, and A7..A0 vary from all 0s to all 1s; converting those endpoint bit patterns to hex gives F800 through F9FF.
